proposal.utterance: Classify 'the status of being a legal person'.

entities.label: LegalPersonhood
entities.rationale: The status of being a legal person is a quality: a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (a person, corporation, or other entity) and is a measurable, attributable property of that bearer at a time. It is not externally grounded by social role-assignment alone in the way a Role is (BFO_0000023), nor is it a disposition (BFO_0000016); rather it is a determinate status-quality that the bearer either has or lacks. BFO Quality (BFO_0000019) is the most precise fit for a status-as-quality in BFO 2020 social ontology practice.

relations.rationale: LegalPersonhood is a subclass of BFO Quality, inheriting the axiom that every instance inheres in exactly one bearer.

open_questions: Should LegalPersonhood be typed as a Role (BFO_0000023) instead, on the grounds that legal personhood is externally conferred by a legal system rather than being an intrinsic quality of the bearer? Role captures socially/institutionally grounded statuses; Quality captures intrinsic or measurable attributes. The choice turns on whether you treat legal personhood as intrinsic-to-bearer or as purely extrinsically assigned.

Is LegalPersonhood best modeled as a class (the kind 'legal-personhood status') or should a specific instance—e.g., the legal personhood of a particular corporation—be the focus? The current proposal mints a class.
Should LegalPersonhood be related to the existing working:LegalRight or working:LegalObligation classes as a precondition or grounding quality? If so, what relation should capture that dependency?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'the status of being a legal person' picks out a specifically dependent continuant: something that inheres in a bearer and characterises it at a time. Within BFO 2020, specifically dependent continuants divide into Qualities (BFO_0000019), Roles (BFO_0000023), and Dispositions (BFO_0000016). A Role is appropriate when the status is purely externally grounded by social/institutional recognition; a Quality is appropriate when the status is a determinate, attributable property of the bearer. Legal personhood sits on the boundary: it is institutionally conferred, which argues for Role, but it is also a standing attribute of the bearer (they have it or they do not, at any given time) that grounds further rights and obligations, which argues for Quality. Following standard BFO-based legal ontology practice (e.g., DOLCE+DnS and OWL treatments of legal status), I propose LegalPersonhood as a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019), representing the determinate status-property that inheres in the bearer. The open questions flag the Role alternative for human adjudication.
